description: See C, C++ and Python code as a live circuit: blocks for folders, files, classes and functions; wires where calls, threads and data flow like current. Compile errors turn red with their impact; Run & Trace replays threads and values.
cfg.defaultLevel: Abstraction level shown first. `auto` picks the finest level that stays readable.
cfg.layout: `circuit`: left-to-right with orthogonal wires. `network`: top-down with curved links.
cfg.flowMode: Electric flow animation on wires: `all`, only for the `focus`ed selection, or `off`.
cfg.maxParticles: Upper bound for animated charges on screen (lower = lighter).
cfg.guesses: Show links resolved by name only (drawn dashed).
cfg.followCursor: Pulse the block under the editor cursor.
cfg.exclude: Glob patterns of files and folders to skip.
cfg.maxFiles: Maximum number of source files to analyze.
cfg.includePaths: Extra include directories (workspace-relative) for `#include` resolution. `compile_commands.json` is read automatically.
cfg.workers: Parser worker threads. `0` = automatic (CPU cores − 1, max 4).
trust.description: Static analysis works everywhere. Compile checks and Run & Trace execute your compiler and program, so they need a trusted workspace.
cfg.verifyMode: When to compile-check the workspace with the real toolchain (`gcc`/`clang -fsyntax-only`, Python `compile()`). Broken blocks turn red and the impact spreads along the wires.
cfg.verifyMode.onOpenAndSave: Check on open, then re-check the affected translation units on every save.
cfg.verifyMode.onOpen: Check once when the circuit opens.
cfg.verifyCc: C compiler for checks and Run & Trace. Empty = `$CC`, then `cc`, `gcc`, `clang`.
cfg.verifyPython: Python 3 interpreter for checks and Run & Trace. Empty = `python3`, then `python` on PATH (the Python extension's selected interpreter is not picked up yet).
cfg.verifyCcdb: Use the flags from `compile_commands.json` when the project has one.
cfg.verifyEditor: Also mark errors reported by language servers (C/C++, clangd, Pylance…).
cfg.runEntry: What Run & Trace starts: a Python file, or a C/C++ file containing `main`. Empty = the active editor's entry point, or pick from a list.
cfg.runEnv: Extra environment variables for the traced program.
cfg.runBuildFlags: Extra compile flags when building a C/C++ program for tracing (e.g. `-DUSE_THREADS`).
cfg.runLinkFlags: Extra link flags/libraries for the traced C/C++ build (e.g. `-lm`, `-lssl`). `-pthread` is always added on Linux/macOS.
cfg.runTimeout: Stop the traced program after this many seconds (the trace up to that point is kept).
cfg.runMaxEvents: Detailed events recorded per run; after that only call counts are kept.
cfg.runValues: Record argument/return values and object identities (data tracking). Turn off for lower overhead.
